text: 🇲🇽✊ "For the first time, women are in the Constitution of the Republic — substantive equality is recognized." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Acapulco, Guerrero Substantive equality, equal pay for equal work, and the right to a life free of violence are now constitutional rights. The Women's Rights booklet has 25 million copies in circulation and has been translated into 68 indigenous languages.

🇲🇽✊ "From age 60 we are going to recognize that work women do. Why? For the sole fact of being a woman." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Pensión Mujeres Bienestar delivery, Acapulco The Women's Wellbeing Pension pays 3,100 pesos bimonthly to women aged 60–64, recognizing decades of unpaid care work. Nearly 3 million women receive it nationwide — about 70,000 in Guerrero and 17,955 in Acapulco. At 65, recipients move on to the universal senior pension.

text:
🇲🇽💰 <u>WORLD CUP LEFT MEXICO 65 BILLION PESOS AND 130,900 JOBS</u>

The final tally is in, El Economista reports: Mexico's World Cup generated 65 billion pesos in economic impact and drew 7.8 million travelers between June 8 and July 19 — 3.3 million of them tourists, up 36% from 2025. Sectur's balance counts 130,900 direct jobs across the three host cities, hotel occupancy averaging 66% with 90% peaks on match days, and the AIFA up 18% in international passengers. They said hosting was a vanity expense. The receipts say otherwise.
banner: WORLD CUP: 65BN PESOS, 130,900 JOBS FOR MX

text:
🇲🇽👩 <u>SHEINBAUM DELIVERS WOMEN'S WELLBEING PENSION IN ACAPULCO</u>

In Acapulco, Claudia Sheinbaum handed out Pensión Mujeres Bienestar cards: 3 million women aged 60 to 64 now receive 3,100 pesos every two months across Mexico — 70,000 in Guerrero, 17,955 in Acapulco alone — as recognition of a lifetime of unpaid care work. She also cited 25 million Women's Rights booklets distributed, Centros LIBRE running in 1,000 municipalities on the way to 2,500, and 250,000 women in the Red Nacional de Tejedoras de la Patria. "When women walk together, nothing can stop us."

🇲🇽⚽ <u>NATIONAL TEAMS ARE MAPS OF MIGRATION — DEAL WITH IT</u>

Writing in Contralínea after a World Cup hosted on Mexican soil, Ana María Ibarra reads the tournament as a cartography of migration and mestizaje — and of its backlash: as punctual as the goals came the racist audits, from the abuse hurled at Kylian Mbappé to players whose nationality is questioned "solely by the color of their skin or the origin of their surnames." A month of football proved the opposite of what the far right preaches: no pure nation exists, and none ever did.

text:
🇲🇽🏥 <u>IMSS BUILDS 47 NEW HOSPITALS: 7 OPEN, 21 UNDER CONSTRUCTION</u>

Mexico's Social Security Institute is running one of the biggest hospital expansions in its history: 47 new hospitals during Sheinbaum's term — 7 already operating, 21 under construction, and 10 more opening within the next 10 months, IMSS director Zoé Robledo reported at the morning conference. The goal: more medical capacity, closer to where people actually live.

🇲🇽💧 <u>LA PAROTA DAM CANCELLED FOR GOOD — ACAPULCO GETS WELLS INSTEAD</u>

Claudia Sheinbaum confirmed in Acapulco that the La Parota dam — resisted by Guerrero's communities for two decades — was cancelled in May "because it affected the community too much," and on the same land Mexico is now building radial wells and elevated tanks to gravity-feed water to the port's neighborhoods. Also underway: new pumps on the Papagayo River, river dredging, and replacement of the potable water networks wrecked by hurricanes Otis and John. The megadam died; the water is coming anyway.
banner: LA PAROTA DAM DEAD, WELLS FOR ACAPULCO

text:
🇲🇽⚖️ <u>MEXICO'S SUPREME COURT TAKES UP EUTHANASIA</u>

Mexico's Supreme Court accepted amparo 147/2026 and will study whether the ban on euthanasia and medically assisted death is unconstitutional — a case brought by Silvia García Castañeda, 69, diagnosed with terminal breast cancer, now in the hands of Minister Lenia Batres. A citizen initiative, Ley Trasciende, backed by senators across parties, would write euthanasia into the General Health Law and repeal article 166 Bis 21 that prohibits it. "I love life," García told La Jornada in her first interview with a media outlet. "But with my diagnosis I face death head-on and I want to die in peace, without pain, without suffering. I have the right to exercise my autonomy and my dignity."
